body.statement: Coverage for the current spec (lookback 5) is exact and small. Each symbol contributes 62 observed unadjusted closes over 2026-05-06..2026-07-31 with zero duplicate keys and zero invalid/null closes, and common_dates equals union_dates (62), so all three series share the same 62 observed dates. A signal at close t uses close[t] and close[t-5], i.e. 6 trailing rows, so the first 5 rows per symbol are excluded as insufficient past observations, leaving 57 eligible signals; exactly 56 of those have a next observed close, so the 2026-07-31 signal (last observed row) is calculable but has no execution observation.

body.statement: Applicability constraints from the frozen contract: every score input must be an observation at or before close t and execution is no earlier than the next observed close, so the final-row signal is calculable but not executable and these observations are exploratory development data, never a holdout. Windows count past observed rows with no filling, and the observed union is not an exchange calendar - all three series skip from 2026-06-18 to 2026-06-22 - so a 5-row lookback spans variable calendar time and date absences must not be read as market closures, suspensions or corporate actions. The download is a current retrieval, not a vintage archive, so point-in-time availability is enforced by rule rather than observed.

The baseline score is a raw 5-observation simple return and its dispersion is symbol-specific: sample SD of the score is 0.042777151396309596 for 300750.XSHE and 0.0402658932201447 for 601318.XSHG versus 0.027943663754569577 for 600036.XSHG, tracking one-observation return SD of 0.02520900080828789, 0.019867351566759856 and 0.012242446444137979 and max absolute one-observation returns of 0.07121171770972035, 0.06406368460955258 and 0.02537274391838862. Cross-symbol comparison of raw scores therefore mixes signal strength with symbol volatility level; the sources contain no forward labels, so no harm or benefit of this scale difference is demonstrated.

body.statement: Testable but unproven hypothesis: the observed symbol-specific score scale motivates at most one alternative spec - normalization realized_volatility with a short volatility_window (e.g. 5), which divides the trailing return by trailing daily-return SD times sqrt(lookback) - to put the three names on a common score scale for later independent evaluation. Explicit limits: it adds a parameter and its own warmup exclusions (the volatility window requires additional past observed rows and positive trailing volatility to be defined), does not make an annual Sharpe ratio and does not remove systematic risk; descriptive score differences cannot establish superiority, and with no forward labels in this window any benefit must be shown by a separate future evaluation that is out of scope. A coherent alternative is to retain the raw baseline, whose coverage (57 eligible signals per symbol) is already characterized.

body.rationale: Chosen revision: keep lookback 5, direction +1 and no return-magnitude eligibility bound from the baseline, and add normalization realized_volatility with volatility_window 5. The motivation is the supported normalization finding: baseline score sample SDs of 0.042777151396309596 (300750.XSHE), 0.027943663754569577 (600036.XSHG) and 0.0402658932201447 (601318.XSHG) track one-observation return SDs of 0.02520900080828789, 0.012242446444137979 and 0.019867351566759856, so raw cross-symbol score comparison mixes signal strength with symbol volatility level. The research question follows directly from that evidence: whether scaling the trailing return by local realized volatility yields a score dimension in which the three names can be compared and later evaluated together. Coverage consequence of the added parameter on this frozen sample is nil: inspection of this exact spec reports per symbol 62 observed closes, 6 closes required per signal (the warmup exclusion count is 5, one less than the 6 required closes; 0 additional exclusions), 62 minus 5 equals 57 eligible signals, and 57 minus the single last row with no next observed close equals 56 signals with a next observed close, identical to the baseline counts. Score-scale consequence is an observed change only: 171 score rows changed and score sample SDs moved to approximately 1.13 (300750.XSHE), 1.74 (600036.XSHG) and 1.56 (601318.XSHG). This changed scale is not demonstrated improvement: dispersion remains symbol-specific after normalization, so equalized cross-symbol comparability is itself unproven, and the frozen sources contain no forward labels, so no benefit over the baseline can be shown here; per the research contract, inspection and adopt/retain are in scope while demonstrating benefit belongs to a separate future evaluation. Retaining the raw baseline was a coherent option; the revision is adopted because it targets the documented scale-mixing at zero observed coverage cost on this sample, not because it is proven better.
